findings.fact: PDC proton assignments and C3 hydrogen exchange in PDC/OMA at the stated pH and incubation times are chemical identification support.
OMA-to-KCH without added LigU was observed after about six hours at pH9.7 in 10%D2O with0.5uM LigI. Unknown3.60ppm signal is explicitly unassigned.
PDC/OMA absorption comparison is an assay calibration at pH10 and30C.
Displayed LigU reference is Q0KJL4; prior complete manual transcription gives357 residues exactly matching issuing KA1 sequence.
LigI hydrolysis product OMA and its borohydride/borodeuteride reductions have distinct NMR assignments.
LigI/LigU at pH9.2 yields assigned OMA/KCH mixture; reductions at pH8.2/8.4 support product identification; glycerol and unknown singlet are not route metabolites.
LigK condenses pyruvate to HMG at pH7.3; added LigJ produces a dehydration product15 with C3/C4 change.

limits: SI provides reference alignment but no complete expression/tag/cleavage methods.

findings.fact: Four6DWV LigJ subunits show a mononuclear zinc center ligated by His8,His10,His178 and water, with chain-dependent distances.
At pH8 in10%D2O, LigI/LigU/LigJ produce PDC/OMA/KCH/CHA equilibrium mixture; reported CHA/KCH ratio3.4. Spectra identify the KCH conjugated keto substrate separately from OMA.

findings.fact: Studied LigJ is explicitly Sphingobium sp.SYK6,Q9KWL6,assigned KCH hydratase; neighboring SSN enzymes do not establish this activity by similarity.
Reversible hydration is drawn from KCH to CHA with water addition; CHA hydroxyl in this scheme has no wedge stereobond.
6DXQ product ligand coordinates zinc in LigJ; related enzyme panels illustrate other catalytic scaffolds.
LigJ alignment is assigned Q9KWL6 and relates characterized COG2159 proteins.
LigJ panel shows zinc and bound water. Caption says6DXQ although FigureS1 states the substrate-free illustration uses6DWV.
